methodological_rigor.justification: The study is a two-cohort observational analysis (a physician-discretion pilot cohort of 85 patients and a retrospective expanded cohort of 465 patients) without a contemporaneous control group or counterfactual comparison to alternative in-network panels, so claims about "expanding treatment options" are largely descriptive. Actionability is defined post hoc using OncoKB levels and broad criteria (eg, indication-matched variants, TMB-H/MSI-H, and potential germline findings), and several key feature-attribution analyses are explicitly not performed in the expanded cohort (eg, which patients were reclassified by tumor-normal matching or detected solely via RNA-seq/liquid reflex). Case studies illustrate plausible clinical impact (eg, MSI status reclassification with tumor-normal matching; reflex liquid biopsy after tissue failure), but selection and ascertainment biases are likely given referral at clinician discretion and partial manual chart review for only a subset (72/85) of the pilot cohort. Statistical analysis is limited to proportions and counts with no uncertainty intervals, no adjustment for confounding, and no sensitivity analyses beyond narrative limitations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: By design this is an observational case-series/retrospective cohort description of testing yields and downstream matches (pilot cohort January–July 2022; expanded cohort March 2019–March 2023) rather than an interventional trial, supporting Oxford LoE 4. The work is directly relevant to community oncology workflows because it reports the frequency of potentially actionable findings (49.4% in the pilot; 31% in the expanded cohort) and documents concrete clinical implications such as therapy eligibility (eg, MSI-H enabling immunotherapy consideration; PIK3CA enabling alpelisib plus fulvestrant) and trial matching/enrollment through the TIME program. Endpoints are primarily surrogate/process outcomes (actionable biomarker detection and trial matching) rather than clinical outcomes like OS/PFS, but the translational path to decision-making is explicit in the results and case studies.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the closest fit because the manuscript reports two observational cohorts with defined inclusion windows, test types (xT/xF/xR), and operational definitions of "potentially actionable" based on OncoKB levels and germline classification criteria. The methods specify cohort timeframes, sample sizes, and key definitions (eg, TMB-H defined as ≥10 mutations/Mb; OncoKB Levels 1–3), and results provide clear numerators/denominators and workflow descriptions (eg, 87 patients notified of 120 trials; three enrolled). However, several checklist-level details are thin or deferred to appendices/figures not available here (eg, full cohort characteristics, handling of missingness beyond noting subsets like 72/85 for prior authorization review), and there is no prospective protocol registration or prespecified analysis plan described. Data/code sharing is limited to statements that data were deidentified before analyses and no repository, dataset identifier, or analysis code availability is provided in the normalized text.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript primarily provides an incremental, practice-focused demonstration that adding CGP features (tumor-normal matching, RNA-seq, liquid biopsy reflex, trial matching) can identify additional actionable findings and avoid misclassification (eg, CHIP vs tumor variant) in a community network. The core concepts and feature benefits are already established in the cited background (eg, tumor-normal for somatic calling/TMB; RNA classifiers for CUP; liquid biopsy complementarity), and the novel contribution is mostly the specific real-world yield/illustrative case studies in this setting. The expanded cohort analysis explicitly cannot attribute many findings to specific advanced features, which further limits claims of distinct novelty beyond descriptive implementation experience.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally clear and well organized, with a methods section that spells out the two cohorts, the testing modalities (xT/xF/xR), and the operational definitions used for actionability. Results are presented with concrete numbers and accessible case studies that connect assay features to clinical decisions (eg, tissue failure triggering reflex liquid biopsy; tumor-normal reclassification affecting MSI status). Some sections read like a product-feature narrative and lean heavily on figures/appendices not visible in the normalized corpus, which can make it harder to independently verify cohort details and trial-enrollment specifics from text alone. Overall, the abstract and section flow accurately reflect the study aims and descriptive outcomes.

key_strengths: Clear two-cohort design with explicit time windows and sample sizes (pilot N=85; expanded N=465) and transparent operational definitions for actionability (OncoKB Levels 1–3; TMB-H threshold; germline classification criteria).

Concrete, clinically interpretable case studies linking CGP features to decisions (eg, MSI status reclassification via tumor-normal matching; reflex liquid biopsy after insufficient tissue; CHIP reclassification avoiding inappropriate therapy).
Includes downstream workflow signal beyond biomarkers alone by reporting trial matching and enrollment through an AI-enabled program (87 notified; three enrolled; activation time reported).
key_concerns: No control group or comparative effectiveness design, so the claim that CGP "expanded treatment options" is not causally supported and may reflect referral/selection effects.
Limited statistical treatment (mostly counts/proportions without uncertainty intervals) and no confounding adjustment or prespecified analysis plan.

Feature-attribution is incomplete in the expanded cohort (the manuscript explicitly did not evaluate which patients benefited from specific advanced features such as liquid reflex, MSI/TMB reclassification, or RNA-seq-only fusion detection).
Reproducibility posture is weak in the provided text: no dataset accessions, code availability, or analytic workflow details sufficient for external replication.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a clinically relevant, clearly written observational implementation report with illustrative cases, but it lacks a comparative design and robust statistical/reproducibility elements needed for higher-tier acceptance; substantial revisions would be required even for a low-tier oncology venue.
